body.statement:
Suppose that the constructed law \(P^{\star}\) obeys the displayed fourth-moment envelope, that is,
\[
 \max_{1\le g\le3}\max_{1\le t\le3}
 E_{P_O^{\star}}[|Y_t|^4\mid G=g]\le M_4.
\]
Then the corrected PT vector is \(q_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})=(0,0)^{\prime}\), its profiled normal \(R_{\mathrm{PT}}\) has rank one, and \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M_I\). The uniquely identified SC weights are \((1/2,1/2)\), while minimizing the PT Gram criterion over donor weights summing to one gives inverse-change-variance weights \((4/5,1/5)\). The exact efficiency bounds are
\[
 V_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})=\frac{42}{5},\qquad
 V_{\mathrm{SC}}(P^{\star})=\frac{1625}{184},\qquad
 V_U(P^{\star})=\frac{39}{4},
\]
and hence
\[
 V_U(P^{\star})-V_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})=\frac{27}{20},\qquad
 V_U(P^{\star})-V_{\mathrm{SC}}(P^{\star})=\frac{169}{184}.
\]
The union QP fixes the final donor coefficients at \((1/2,1/2)\); its required SC preperiod-normal coefficient differs from the SC oracle coefficient, so both one-sided Gram discrepancies are strictly positive. The same strict inequalities hold on a relatively open region preserving the fourth-moment envelope, full rank, unequal positive donor-change variances, and unequal SC and PT-oracle weights.
body.justification: The witness proves that the adaptation frontier has empirical content and is not an algebraic relabelling of the PT-efficient score.
body.gap: ChenSantAnnaXie2025 shows covariance-optimal PT weighting, and SunXieZhang2025 identifies SC weights from preperiod means, but neither paper exhibits a legal intersection region where the two canonical gradients differ and union regularity is strictly costly.
body.consumer: The witness is a calibration design for simulations that test software implementing the union quadratic program and its standard errors.
body.proof_tex:
There is one stratum and every group has probability \(1/3\).  Hence
\(p_X(x)=1\geq\kappa_0\) and \(p_g(x)=1/3>\epsilon_0\), where the strict
inequality follows from \(\epsilon_0<1/(J+1)=1/3\).  No anticipation holds by
construction.  The untreated final-period changes of all three conditional
mean paths are zero.  Therefore conditional parallel trends holds and
\[
 D=(0,0)^{\prime},\qquad \delta_1^0=0,\qquad
 q_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})
 =\delta_1^0\mathbf 1_2-D=(0,0)^{\prime}.
 \tag{10}
\]
The augmented donor matrix and the treated preperiod target are
\[
 B=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\-1&1\\-2&2\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 a=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 B^{\prime}B=\begin{pmatrix}6&-4\\-4&6\end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{11}
\]
The eigenvalues of \(B^{\prime}B\) are \(2\) and \(10\).  Thus
\(\lambda_{\min}(B^{\prime}B)=2\geq\kappa_0\), since \(\kappa_0<1\), and the
SC rank condition holds.  Solving \(Bw=a\) gives the unique vector
\[
 w=(1/2,1/2)^{\prime}.
 \tag{12}
\]
It also reproduces the treated untreated mean in period three because
\((-2)/2+2/2=0\).  Thus the synthetic-mean restriction holds in all three
periods.  Together with the fourth-moment inequality assumed in the
proposition, (10)--(12) prove \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M_I\).  For completeness,
the largest fourth moment among the fixed untreated cells is \(68\), and the
treated observed final cell has fourth moment
\((\tau^{\star})^4+6(\tau^{\star})^2+1\); this follows from
\(E[(m+\sigma U)^4]=m^4+6m^2\sigma^2+\sigma^4\) for a Rademacher variable
\(U\).  The displayed envelope assumption is therefore precisely the needed
moment qualification.

For \(g,t\in\{1,2,3\}\), define
\[
 z_{g,t}=3\mathbf 1\{G=g\}\varepsilon_{g,t}.
 \tag{13}
\]
For an arbitrary regular score \(s\), differentiation of a conditional cell
mean gives
\[
 \dot\mu_{g,t}(s)
 =E_{P_O^{\star}}[3\mathbf 1\{G=g\}
   (Y_t-\mu_{g,t})s]
 =E_{P_O^{\star}}[z_{g,t}s].
 \tag{14}
\]
Thus \(z_{g,t}\) is its mean-zero influence variable.  Disjoint group
indicators and independent centered innovations make the nine variables in
(13) pairwise orthogonal.  Their variances, listed by time within group, are
\[
 (3,3,3),\qquad (3,3/2,3/2),\qquad (6,6,6).
 \tag{15}
\]

By the tangent normal form, the PT influence face can be parameterized by a
donor weight \(v\in\mathbb R\) as
\[
 \psi_{\mathrm{PT}}(v)
 =(z_{1,3}-z_{1,2})
  -v(z_{2,3}-z_{2,2})
  -(1-v)(z_{3,3}-z_{3,2}).
 \tag{16}
\]
The two donor-change variances are respectively \(3\) and \(12\), and the
treated-change variance is \(6\).  Orthogonality in (15) therefore gives
\[
 \|\psi_{\mathrm{PT}}(v)\|_0^2
 =6+3v^2+12(1-v)^2.
 \tag{17}
\]
The derivative of the donor part is \(30v-24\), and its second derivative is
\(30>0\).  Its unique minimizer is \(v=4/5\), whence
\[
 V_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})
 =6+3(4/5)^2+12(1/5)^2
 =\frac{42}{5}.
 \tag{18}
\]
Moreover, for \(J=2\), \(A_{\mathrm{PT}}\) has rank one.  The sole donor-change
contrast has variance \(3+12=15>0\), so the profiled PT normal Gram matrix has
rank exactly one.

We next compute the SC face.  The vector
\(u=(0,-2,1)^{\prime}\) spans \(\ker(B^{\prime})\) and satisfies
\(u^{\prime}u=5\).  At the exact equality \(a=Bw\), differentiation of the
normal equations \(B^{\prime}(Bw-a)=0\) gives
\[
 \dot w=(B^{\prime}B)^{-1}B^{\prime}(\dot a-\dot B\,w).
 \tag{19}
\]
Since the donor final-period mean row is \((-2,2)\), direct multiplication
using (11) yields
\[
 -(-2,2)\dot w
 =(0,-2/5,-4/5)(\dot a-\dot B\,w).
 \tag{20}
\]
Combining (20) with the direct final-period derivatives of
\(\theta_{\mathrm{SC}}\), the unrestricted SC gradient has cell-mean
coefficients, ordered by time within groups one, two, and three,
\[
 (-2/5,-4/5,1),\qquad
 (1/5,2/5,-1/2),\qquad
 (1/5,2/5,-1/2).
 \tag{21}
\]

Differentiating
\(r_{\mathrm{SC}}=(I_3-B(B^{\prime}B)^{-1}B^{\prime})a\) at \(a=Bw\)
gives
\[
 \dot r_{\mathrm{SC}}
 =(I_3-B(B^{\prime}B)^{-1}B^{\prime})(\dot a-\dot B\,w).
 \tag{22}
\]
The range of the projector in (22) is the one-dimensional span of \(u\).
Thus the SC normal span is generated by
\(\rho=u^{\prime}(\dot a-\dot B\,w)\).  Adding \(\beta\rho\) to (21) changes
only the preperiod coefficients.  Using (15), their contribution to the
variance is
\[
\begin{aligned}
 Q(\beta)
 &=3(-2/5-2\beta)^2+3(-4/5+\beta)^2
   +3(1/5+\beta)^2+\frac32(2/5-\beta/2)^2\\
 &\quad+6(1/5+\beta)^2+6(2/5-\beta/2)^2\\
 &=\frac{207}{8}\beta^2+\frac35\beta+\frac{99}{25}.
\end{aligned}
 \tag{23}
\]
Because \(207/8>0\), completing the square gives
\[
 \beta^{\mathrm{or}}=-\frac{4}{345},
 \qquad
 \min_{\beta}Q(\beta)=\frac{91}{23}.
 \tag{24}
\]
The final-period contribution from (21) is
\[
 3+\frac14\frac32+\frac14 6=\frac{39}{8}.
\]
It follows that
\[
 V_{\mathrm{SC}}(P^{\star})
 =\frac{39}{8}+\frac{91}{23}
 =\frac{1625}{184}.
 \tag{25}
\]

Every SC normal in (22) is supported on preperiod mean coordinates.  Hence
every element of the SC influence face has final donor coefficients
\((-1/2,-1/2)\).  Equality with the PT representative (16) forces
\(v=1/2\).  Equality of the preperiod coefficients in (16) and (21) then
forces \(\beta=-1/5\); substitution in (21) gives
\[
 (0,-1,1),\qquad (0,1/2,-1/2),\qquad (0,1/2,-1/2).
 \tag{26}
\]
Conversely, (26) is exactly \(\psi_{\mathrm{PT}}(1/2)\), so the two faces do
intersect.  The final donor coefficients already force the only PT parameter
to be \(v=1/2\), and hence the intersection is the singleton (26).  By
\(\mathrm{thm{:}union\text{-}envelope}\), this unique common representative is
\(\phi_U\).  Equations (15) and (26) give
\[
 V_U(P^{\star})
 =6+3(1/2)^2+12(1/2)^2
 =\frac{39}{4}.
 \tag{27}
\]

The PT oracle has \(v=4/5\ne1/2\), so it does not belong to the SC face.  The
SC oracle has \(\beta=-4/345\ne-1/5\), so it is not the unique common element
and therefore does not belong to the PT face.  By
\(\mathrm{thm{:}oracle\text{-}adaptation\text{-}frontier}\), both one-sided
Gram discrepancies are strictly positive.  Subtracting (18) and (25) from
(27) gives
\[
 V_U(P^{\star})-V_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})=\frac{27}{20},
 \qquad
 V_U(P^{\star})-V_{\mathrm{SC}}(P^{\star})=\frac{169}{184}.
 \tag{28}
\]

It remains to justify the neighborhood assertion.  On the finite-support
model, all entries of the displayed Gram matrices are continuous functions of
cell probabilities, conditional means, and conditional second moments.
Matrix inversion in (19), the unique quadratic minimizers in (17) and (23),
and their minimized values are continuous wherever the positive rank margins
in (11), (17), and (23) persist.  At \(P^{\star}\), the cell probabilities and
nonzero eigenvalues are positive, both donor-change variances are positive and
unequal, the SC and PT-oracle weights are unequal, and both gaps in (28) are
strict.  Each property therefore persists in a sufficiently small
neighborhood relative to \(\mathcal M_I\).  Intersecting that neighborhood
with the set satisfying the displayed fourth-moment envelope produces the
claimed relatively open region in the envelope-constrained model, including
the relative topology when the envelope is attained at its boundary.
